instruction.text: Sort the characteristics into the correct category.
Equality and inequality are closely connected to political systems. Find the correct title for each paragraph.

atoms.b:
((Equality_and_Democracy))
Democracies are generally based on the idea that all citizens should have equal rights, freedoms and opportunities. Although real democracies are not always perfectly equal, they aim to protect individual rights and reduce inequality through fair laws and political participation.

((Inequality_and_Totalitarianism))
Totalitarian systems concentrate power in the hands of a single ruler or government. They limit freedom, control information and often create inequalities by giving certain groups more rights, resources or privileges than others.

((The_Paradox_of_Equality))
Interestingly, some societies claim to create complete equality but achieve it by restricting personal freedom and enforcing strict control. For example, a government might require everyone to wear the same clothes and live in identical houses. While this appears to create equality, citizens have no freedom to make their own choices.

instruction.text: Read the example and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Everyone wears the same clothes, earns the same salary and follows the same daily schedule. However, speaking against the totalitarian government is strictly forbidden.

atoms.a: Which statement best describes this society?
b: ++Equal treatment can exist alongside a lack of individual freedom.
A perfect example of an equal society.

instruction.text: Read the example. What is the main idea of this society?

atoms.text: Every ten years, jobs, homes and salaries are assigned randomly through a national lottery. This system prevents inherited privilege, but people cannot choose careers that match their interests or talents.

b: ++Equality is promoted by removing personal choice.
Wealth is passed from parents to children.
People have complete freedom to shape their future.

instruction.text: Read the example. Why might many people consider this society utopian?

atoms.text: Citizens work only four hours a day because robots perform most jobs. A universal basic income guarantees food, housing and healthcare for everyone. People spend most of their time learning, creating art, volunteering or participating in democracy.

b: ++Basic needs are guaranteed, allowing people to pursue personal interests.
Education is available only to a small group.

instruction.text: Read the example. What is the main source of inequality in this society?

atoms.text: Wealthy parents can pay to edit their babies' genes before they are born. These children are healthier, more intelligent and less likely to develop diseases. Families who cannot afford gene editing have natural children, who often face discrimination when applying for schools and jobs.

b: ++Wealth allows some families to give their children genetic advantages.
The government chooses every child's genes.
Everyone has equal access to genetic technology.
